version.changelog: Moved to vmware-skills GitHub org; MCP Registry namespace → io.github.vmware-skills. Links updated.

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent VMware audit and policy helper, but it documents a broad switch that can disable policy enforcement across high-impact VMware operations.

dimensions.detail: Local audit storage in ~/.vmware/audit.db, rules in ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, and read-only agent detection from environment variables are disclosed and fit the audit purpose; users should still treat audit records as restricted operational data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is through uv/uvx of the vmware-policy package, and the submitted artifact contains documentation only with no executable scripts; however, it depends on a community package rather than bundled inspectable source code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime guidance is mostly clear, but the bypass is presented as a troubleshooting/environment option without strong break-glass scoping, authorization, time limits, or prominent warnings; audit export is also documented without warning that logs may contain sensitive operational metadata.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent local audit state and hot-reloaded policy rules, which is expected for its purpose, but policy enforcement can be disabled by an ordinary environment variable while operations continue.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is unified audit logging, policy enforcement, and sanitization for VMware skills, but the artifacts document VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 as a global policy-check bypass that can affect all wrapped operations, including high and critical infrastructure actions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing in production. The audit and policy functions are useful and disclosed, but do not rely on this as a strong enforcement boundary unless you can prevent agents and users from setting VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED, protect ~/.vmware/audit.db and exported logs, and verify policy rules are present and enforced in your environment.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed as a material concern: a policy/audit infrastructure skill documents VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 as a broad bypass, which is not sufficiently scoped for high-impact VMware operations even though bypassed operations are logged.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed for the capabilities reference: the bypass disables all policy checks and is documented without admin-only controls or emergency-only framing.
[SQP-2] expected: Partially accepted for audit export: exporting audit logs is purpose-aligned, but the documentation should warn that exported records can reveal operational metadata and should be protected.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed for the CLI reference: the environment-variable bypass is documented in user-facing command documentation without strong warnings or compensating controls.
